purpose: Expanded challenge set written to probe paraphrase transfer and plausible same-topic distractors. Cases are simulated author judgments, not independent human ground truth; failed cases remain visible and labels must not be retuned to force passing.

cases.query: A policy protects residents in one district but leaves neighboring families bearing the cost. How should leaders weigh the options?

direct.title: Ethical Trade-offs When Repairing Harm
direct.text: When a remedy benefits one group while burdening another, decision-makers should compare alternatives, identify who bears each burden, protect rights, and explain the reasons for the choice.

distractor.title: Community Belonging and Group Affiliation
distractor.text: Explore identity, authenticity, and how people maintain belonging while navigating group expectations.

cases.query: People say the settlement closes the case but leaves their losses unaddressed. What should happen next?

direct.title: Restorative Justice and Meaningful Repair
direct.text: Meaningful repair listens to harmed people, understands actual losses, and revises restitution or redress when the proposed remedy does not meet their needs.

distractor.title: Transparent Governance
distractor.text: Institutions document decisions, publish reasons, and report governance outcomes to the public.

cases.query: Members share an aim, but the meeting keeps circling around competing first moves. What process could help them choose?

direct.title: Collective Sense-making SOP: Decentralized Consensus
direct.text: When members disagree about priorities, make each person's reasons visible, identify the shared outcome, compare proposals, and test a small reversible action together.

distractor.title: General Governance Principles
distractor.text: Governance describes institutions, policies, and broad principles for public decision-making.

cases.query: An organization ignored warnings, and the damage people predicted happened. What is a responsible response now?

direct.title: Accountability After Harmful Decisions
direct.text: Responsible decision-makers review warnings and evidence, acknowledge responsibility for foreseeable harm, explain what went wrong, hear affected people, and revise safeguards.

distractor.title: Ethical Trade-offs and Decision Criteria
distractor.text: Decision-makers compare alternatives, weigh competing values, and explain difficult choices when priorities conflict.

cases.query: A few confident voices shape the meeting while quieter members barely get heard. How can the process be balanced?

direct.title: Power, Fairness, and Meaningful Participation
direct.text: Notice unequal power, protect the voice of less powerful participants, create meaningful opportunities to contribute, and make participation fair.

distractor.title: Personal Productivity and Morning Routines
distractor.text: Build a daily routine, organize tasks, and maintain personal productivity habits.

cases.query: Someone feels they must hide important parts of themselves to remain accepted by their community. How might they think about this tension?

direct.title: Community Belonging and Group Affiliation
direct.text: Explore belonging, authenticity, and identity when personal integrity comes into tension with group expectations and community membership.
